t: A Seljuk sultanate that ruled central Anatolia from Konya for over two centuries after the Byzantine defeat at Manzikert.
Its sultans built a Persianate court and a trade network of ports and caravanserais linking the Mediterranean and Black Sea.
Defeat by the Mongols at Köse Dağ in 1243 made it a vassal state, and it dissolved into the beyliks that included the Ottomans.
dyk: The Seljuks of Rum built more than a hundred caravanserais along Anatolia’s roads, some so large and fortified that they resemble castles.
ev: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish establishes Seljuk rule in western Anatolia
The First Crusade takes Nicaea and defeats Kilij Arslan I at Dorylaeum
Kilij Arslan II defeats Manuel I Komnenos at Myriokephalon
Kaykhusraw I captures the port of Antalya
Kayqubad I takes Alanya and fortifies it
The Mongols crush the Seljuk army at the Battle of Köse Dağ
The poet and mystic Rumi dies in Konya
The last sultan, Mesud II, dies and the sultanate lapses
